papers.title: Selective laser melting of stainless-steel/nano-hydroxyapatite composites for medical applications: Microstructure, element distribution, crack and mechanical properties
papers.first_author_affiliation: State Key Lab of Materials Processing and Die&Mould Technology, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan 430074, China

corresponding_authors.name: Qingsong Wei
corresponding_authors.affiliation: State Key Lab of Materials Processing and Die&Mould Technology, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan 430074, China

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及医用金属/陶瓷复合材料的选区激光熔化，但未直接研究多孔结构、应力遮挡或疲劳性能，对用户方向有间接参考价值。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not investigate porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue behavior, or as-built surface morphology relevant to osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发用于医疗植入物的不锈钢/纳米羟基磷灰石复合材料
summary_zh.method: 通过选区激光熔化制备复合材料，分析微观结构和元素分布
summary_zh.result: 获得了致密的复合结构，但存在裂纹和元素偏析
summary_zh.validation: 通过微观表征和力学测试验证材料性能

summary_en.motivation: To develop stainless-steel/nano-hydroxyapatite composite materials suitable for medical implants via selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Composite samples were fabricated by selective laser melting, and their microstructure, element distribution, and crack formation were analyzed.
summary_en.result: Dense composite structures were achieved, but cracks and element segregation were observed, affecting mechanical properties.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through microstructural characterization and mechanical testing including compression or hardness.

papers.title: Outcome of a modular tapered uncemented titanium femoral stem in revision hip arthroplasty
papers.first_author_affiliation: Orthopaedic Clinic Koenig-Ludwig-Haus, Center for Musculoskeletal Research, Julius-Maximilians-University Wuerzburg, Brettreichstr. 11, 97074, Wuerzburg, Germany, m-hoberg.klh@uni-wuerzburg.de

corresponding_authors.name: M. Hoberg
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Orthopaedic Clinic Koenig-Ludwig-Haus, Center for Musculoskeletal Research, Julius-Maximilians-University Wuerzburg, Brettreichstr. 11, 97074, Wuerzburg, Germany, m-hoberg.klh@uni-wuerzburg.de

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为临床病例随访研究，未涉及任何生物力学建模或应力遮挡分析。
llm.why_not_core: No finite element modeling, no stress shielding quantification, no micromotion analysis, no implant-bone interface mechanics, and no comparison of intact vs implanted femur.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估模块化锥形非骨水泥股骨柄在翻修髋关节置换术中的临床效果
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析患者术后影像学及功能评分
summary_zh.result: 该假体在翻修术中显示出良好的中期存活率和临床结果
summary_zh.validation: 临床随访及影像学评估

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the clinical outcomes of a modular tapered uncemented titanium femoral stem in revision hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Retrospective analysis of postoperative radiographic and functional scores from a patient cohort.
summary_en.result: The stem demonstrated favorable mid-term survival and clinical outcomes in revision settings.

papers.title: Chemical and Physical Properties and Biocompatibility of Ti–6Al–4V Produced by Electron Beam Rapid Manufacturing and Selective Laser Melting for Biomedical Applications
papers.venue: World Academy of Science, Engineering and Technology, International Journal of Medical and Health Sciences

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了电子束熔炼和选择性激光熔化制造的Ti-6Al-4V的化学物理性质和生物相容性，但未涉及多孔结构、应力遮挡、疲劳性能或表面粗糙度与骨整合的关系。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on general chemical and physical properties and biocompatibility of Ti-6Al-4V produced by EBM and SLM, but does not specifically address porous structures for stiffness matching, stress shielding, or fatigue performance, nor does it quantify surface roughness or as-built morphology in relation to osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 表征增材制造Ti-6Al-4V用于生物医学的性能与生物相容性
summary_zh.method: 使用电子束熔炼和选择性激光熔化制造样品，进行化学物理表征和生物相容性测试
summary_zh.result: 材料满足生物医学应用要求，具有良好的力学性能和细胞相容性
summary_zh.validation: 通过材料力学测试和体外细胞实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To characterize the chemical, physical, and biocompatibility properties of Ti-6Al-4V produced by electron beam melting and selective laser melting for biomedical applications.
summary_en.method: Samples were fabricated via EBM and SLM, followed by chemical analysis, physical property measurements, and in vitro biocompatibility assays.
summary_en.result: The materials exhibited suitable mechanical properties and cytocompatibility for biomedical use.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through mechanical testing and in vitro cell culture experiments.
